neet_che_u03_t03_1.working: By definition (NCERT), lattice enthalpy is the energy required to completely separate one mole of a solid ionic compound into its gaseous ions.

neet_che_u03_t03_2.working: MgO and CaO have 2+/2- ions, so they come first; Mg2+ is smaller than Ca2+, so MgO > CaO. Among the 1+/1- salts, F- is smaller than Cl-, so NaF > NaCl. Order: MgO > CaO > NaF > NaCl.

neet_che_u03_t03_4.working: NaCl has lattice enthalpy +788 kJ/mol. LiF has the smallest ions, so it is the highest among alkali halides. CsI has the largest ions, so it is the lowest. Lattice enthalpy is determined via the Born-Haber cycle.

neet_che_u03_t03_5.working: A is false: lattice enthalpy decreases as interionic distance increases. B is true: higher lattice enthalpy means higher melting point and hardness. C is true: a salt dissolves if hydration enthalpy compensates lattice enthalpy. D is false: it cannot be measured directly and is found indirectly via Born-Haber. E is true: it is proportional to the product of ionic charges. Correct set: B, C, E.
